subtitle.value: A bilingual theory, evidence, and architecture-decision foundation for reasoning about agent systems, with explicit claim states, evidence levels, implementation and validation status, source provenance, and bounded architectural analysis across memory, tools, collaboration, and system evaluation.

A bilingual, source-grounded research observatory tracing artificial intelligence from its intellectual and computational roots to the agentic frontier, using daily observations, weekly hypothesis correction, monthly synthesis, curated source registries, active watchlists, and explicit methodological and governance boundaries.

A dependency-free Python reference implementation for explicit data contracts, canonical JSON and SHA-256 digests, validated probability distributions, KL-divergence measurement, transactional state transitions, reproducible repository checks, and bounded event-recorded orchestration.

A bilingual, source-grounded research observatory for China's artificial-intelligence and agent ecosystem, integrating history, policy, standards, research, open source, industry, infrastructure, applications, and governance through daily observations, weekly hypothesis correction, monthly synthesis, curated sources, and explicit research methodology.

An evidence-aware state-machine framework for research workflows, modeling discovery, analysis, verification, synthesis, and archiving as inspectable transitions with explicit claim, evidence, and conflict structures, runtime policy, checkpoints, recovery identity, provenance, claim verification and transfer, and bounded evidence handoff.

A standard-library Python reference for versioned graph storage and bounded analysis, combining SQLite persistence, synchronized FTS5 lexical search, version deltas, PageRank-derived Shannon entropy, explicit validation, transactional ingestion, and optional bounded reflection hooks.

A standard-library research laboratory for deterministic state, evidence, and edge-native execution, featuring SQLite-backed memory, explicit lifecycle protocols, reproducible ledgers, graph-based structural analysis, and a strict separation between implementation constraints and claims of trust.

An AST-driven research-document compilation engine that treats documents as inspectable artifacts, combining typed Markdown structures, structural-change evidence, cross-document graphs, bounded metadata diagnostics, process disclosure, SARIF interchange, optional RO-Crate packaging, explicit artifact lineage, and multi-format output.

A declarative scientific-figure compilation toolkit with explicit uncertainty semantics, accessibility intent, publisher-target boundaries, claim-to-visual communication audits, dimensional communication coverage, runtime checks, provenance-aware sidecars, and portable figure evidence.

A public portal and research gateway for an edge-first research system, combining bilingual presentation, a deterministic knowledge lifecycle, append-only evidence, provenance-aware validation, reproducible repository maintenance, and independently operated presentation and knowledge-processing layers.

attributes.title: NEXUS CORTEX Life Cycle — welcome-to-github
attributes.description:
Historical executable generation of the NEXUS CORTEX lifecycle workflow for the welcome-to-github research software lineage, recorded from repository state 0b2e45c0b2eff554cf40431ce3c53693d86bc290 on 2026-10-07.

The workflow implements a graph-based, bounded research lifecycle with read-only validation and guarded application paths. It validates runtime contracts and active ledgers, harvests and projects approved external evidence, canonicalizes the active graph, rebuilds and ingests memory, produces bounded lifecycle projections, verifies graph and runtime integrity, checks the permitted write boundary and repository world-line, and applies only a stable and meaningful candidate.

This WorkflowHub record preserves an externally registered historical workflow generation. The canonical implementation history remains in the source Git repository; the corresponding AGI record stores identity, verification and recovery metadata rather than a second executable copy.

attributes.title: NEXUS CORTEX Research Workflows
attributes.description: Research workflows for the NEXUS CORTEX lifecycle architecture, evolving from graph-theoretic models of entities, relations, state projection, verification, and bounded evolution into executable, versioned research workflows. The team currently maintains independent workflow lineages for welcome-to-github and zero-entropy-lab.

attributes.title: Brain Evolution — welcome-to-github
attributes.description: Historical executable precursor of the NEXUS CORTEX research workflow lineage in welcome-to-github, preserved from repository commit a01c6e8df1f5e8ba80726ede6cbdb5de692e8741 on 2026-02-15. This daily GitHub Actions workflow harvested external evidence, produced dated intelligence artifacts, and opened a pull request for human review rather than applying its findings directly. It established an early observe–record–review pattern, but was named Brain Evolution and must not be retrospectively presented as a version of the later NEXUS CORTEX Life Cycle. The canonical executable is .github/workflows/brain_evolution.yml at the recorded Git commit; the AGI lineage record preserves its identity and recovery evidence without containing a second executable copy.
